To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spin-spin coupling constants (125)Te-1H of tellurophenes and divinyltelluride are strongly dependent on the geometry of the molecule, and that the orientational lone pairs of tellurium play a key role in this dependence.

the (125)Te-1H coupling constants of tellurium-containing organic molecules are stereospecific and that the stereospecificity can be used as a tool for the determination of the configuration at the tellurium atom.

the SOPPA method is the method of choice to calculate spin-spin coupling constants in organotelluromolecules, that a new full-electron relativistic basis set for tellurium has to be used, and that conformational averaging and orientational lone pair effects are of prime importance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed study of the spin-spin coupling constants between tellurium and protons.

the development of a reliable methodology for the calculation of indirect spin-spin coupling constant involving tellurium, as well as with the application of the developed methodology to the investigation of the stereochemical properties of organotelluric compounds.
the calculation of indirect spin-spin coupling constant involving tellurium and the development of new basis sets for correlated calculations of spin-coupling constants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the SOPPA method, if relativistic and conformational effects are included, is a reliable tool for the calculation of indirect (125)Te-spin-spin coupling constants, and that the new av3z-J basis set is an excellent basis set choice for the calculation of spin-spin couplings in tellurium containing molecules.

the SOPPA method with the new basis set av3z-J and ZORA relativistic corrections is an ideal method for the accurate prediction of (125) Te-(1)H coupling constants in tellurophene-type molecules, and that the SOPPA results can be further improved by the inclusion of conformational averaging.
the (125)Te NMR spectroscopic properties can be reliably predicted using the SOPPA(CC) level of theory, if the basis sets are properly chosen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the SOPPA method is a reliable tool for the calculation of indirect spin-spin coupling involving tellurium, provided relativistic effects are taken into account and the basis sets are sufficiently flexible.

a combination of the SOPPA method and the av3z-J basis set is a very good choice for the calculation of (H,Te,H) spin-spin coupling constants in medium sized organotallurium molecules, if relativistic corrections are considered.

, for a first time, we have been able to calculate the spin-spin coupling constants in medium-sized organotellur compounds with a high accuracy and to establish a guideline in the stereochemistry of organotellur species.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the SOPPA method is the method of choice in the calculation of indirect nuclear spin-spin coupling constants, in the case of tellurium containing organometallic compounds, if the effects of relativity, conformational averaging and solvent effects are taken into account.
the SOPPA method is a reliable and accurate method for the calculation of spin-spin couplings involving tellurium.

the SOPPA(CC) method is able to provide accurate (125)Te-NMR chemical shifts and spin-spin coupling constants, and that the use of the ZORA Hamiltonian is mandatory for a correct description of the relativistic effects in the spin-spin coupling calculations.
